description:
# Why Fixes ENG-8456 # How This `expo run` command is identical to the `eas build:run` command, where users are presented with a selection of each platform. - Added `src/run/index.ts` command - Combined all flags in the help information, with platform-specific flags underlined
$ expo run --help
$ expo run --device (android)
$ expo run --device (ios)
$ expo run android --help
$ expo run ios --help
# Test Plan See above commands, all flags should be propagated and handled by the original `expo run:android|ios` commands, except `--help`. # Checklist - [ ] Documentation is up to date to reflect these changes (eg: https://docs.expo.dev and README.md). - [ ] Conforms with the [Documentation Writing Style Guide](https://github.com/expo/expo/blob/main/guides/Expo%20Documentation%20Writing%20Style%20Guide.md) - [ ] This diff will work correctly for `npx expo prebuild` & EAS Build (eg: updated a module plugin).

comments.body: After this step, it should print the `expo run:<platform>` command with the same flags. So the user knows what command to run next time. cc @EvanBacon
Seems like we should drop these and just add a tip at the end which tells people to use `run:ios` and `run:android` for more options.
Wrap this whole block with `logCmdError` to ensure error formatting is correct.
If we're doing permissive, then maybe it makes sense to allow a `-p, --platform` flag which can skip the prompt.

The idea behind `permissive` is that we don't need to validate the flags of `expo run:ios` and `expo run:android`. Instead, it just passes the flags through to the proper command.

The `--platform` flag makes sense too, so will definitely add that.
I think that makes sense. But, if we do add `--platform`, we might as well add that flag in this help output, right?
The reason we extracted the argument logic in the other commands was so that we could setup unit tests. Given this command is tied to a native build, it isn’t a spectacular candidate for e2e testing.
Yeah, seems more like a unit test with some mocking it's probably better suited for.

Unfortunately, we can't unit test files using dynamic imports through `await import`. Running into this Jest bug, which seems to be a V8 issue:
  - https://github.com/jestjs/jest/issues/10944
  - https://github.com/aelbore/esbuild-jest/issues/48
  - https://github.com/nodejs/node/issues/36351

Going to write some basic E2E instead.
